correctness.rationale: For x>sqrt(a²+b²), each conditional success implies longitudinal increment Y >= (x²-r²-b²)/(2r)>0, while Y >= -b and E[Y|F1]=0. Thus success probability <= b/(b+t_r) and t_r strictly decreases with the first-step radius r<=a. The exact threshold bound is attained by explicit centered second-step mass q/2,q/2,1-q on (t,±sqrt(b²-t²)) and (-b,0), and independent symmetric first-step signs. Orthogonal first and second steps attain probability one through the critical radius; the triangle inequality handles support. Equality conditions, scalar/symmetric refinements and fixed quadratic proxy optimize by elementary conditional and algebraic steps. All endpoint/equality cases are stated; 3,892 exact-rational finite assertions ran from package paths and are not substituted for infinite proof.

value.rationale: Deterministic per-step bounds are the standard primitive input to concentration inequalities. A complete attained two-step threshold-tail profile is a natural exact model of short-horizon vector-martingale concentration. The result shows a strict one-dimensional versus planar gap and a distinct asymmetric versus conditionally symmetric gap, identifies all optimizing conditional laws in the strict upper regime, and determines exactly when the crude Chebyshev proxy is sharp. These structural phenomena are mathematically motivated and not merely a tiny numerical gain or renaming of a known smooth-moment comparison.
